name: Purply
lede: Purply is a strong magenta-purple from the 2010 xkcd color survey, a casual *-y* coinage on the word *purple* rather than a modifier of any existing compound name.

sections.title: A casual coinage
sections.body: The nearest named colors on file are [[purple-plum]], [[iris-purple]] and [[purple-munsell]], at 4.3, 4.5 and 4.5 ΔE [1][2]. Unlike the modifier compounds elsewhere in the xkcd survey, *purply* adds the informal suffix *-y* directly to the color word, the same pattern as calling something *bluey* or *greeny* [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system's nearest block, strong purple, sits 5.8 units away, closer than some of the batch's other novelty names [2]. In LCH it measures lightness 43, chroma 71, hue 320 degrees, near [[plum]] and [[amethyst]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a color within four units of Purply covering at least one per cent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. As with the other strongly saturated purples, that likely reflects how hard this exact magenta-purple is to reach with historical pigments rather than any property of painting as a whole [3]. In printed English the informal word *purply* appears only sporadically, peaking modestly around 1870, well before this specific hex value was ever recorded [4].
